datagovgR is an R wrapper for the [data.gov.gr](https://www.data.gov.gr/) API. It lets R users, data analysts, academics and students work with Greek open government data programmatically. Queries go to the v1 API at <https://data.gov.gr/api/v1/>.

Currently available endpoint:

-   **"mdg_emvolio"**: COVID-19 vaccination statistics

## 1. Install and load

```{r}
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("elenigvasilaki/datagovgR")
library(datagovgR)
```

## 2. Get and set your API token

You need a personal access token, which you can request at <https://www.data.gov.gr/token>. It is sent by email.

Set it once per session; every query then uses it automatically:

```{r}
set_token("token abcd12344321")

# check which token is set
get_token()
```

To avoid writing the token in your scripts, keep it in your `.Renviron` file (for example `DATAGOVGR_TOKEN=token abcd12344321`) and read it from there:

```{r}
set_token(Sys.getenv("DATAGOVGR_TOKEN"))
```

## 3. Query a dataset

`gov_query()` takes the dataset name and, optionally, a start and an end date (`"YYYY-MM-DD"`):

```{r}
vacc <- gov_query("mdg_emvolio", start_date = "2022-07-04", end_date = "2022-07-11")
```

Either date can be left out. Without dates, the API decides which records it returns:

```{r}
recent <- gov_query("mdg_emvolio", start_date = "2022-07-01")
```

The result is a data frame:

```{r}
str(vacc)
head(vacc)
```

## 4. What happens when something goes wrong

-   No token set: `gov_query()` stops and tells you to use `set_token()`.
-   No dataset given: it stops and asks for a dataset name.
-   No internet connection: it stops with a message to check your connection.
-   Temporary server errors: the request is retried up to three times before giving up. Errors such as an invalid token (401/403) or an unknown dataset (404) stop immediately.
